---
title: "Week 6 — Programs That Make Decisions"
subtitle: "Boolean conditions, comparisons, if/elif/else, and branching"
---

::: {.callout-tip}
## This week's central question

**How can a program choose different actions for different situations?**
:::

## Learning goals

By the end of this week, you should be able to:

1. evaluate simple comparison expressions;
2. explain how a Boolean condition controls a branch;
3. write basic `if`, `if/else`, and `if/elif/else` structures;
4. predict which branch will execute before running code;
5. connect decision rules to domain logic;
6. identify unreachable or incorrectly ordered conditions.

## Connection to Week 5

Last week, programs received data from users.

This week, programs use that information to decide what should happen next.

- analyzing branch order and boundary cases.
